# The App worker's import filter cannot match a docs app entry, so a bundled docs app fails to load

## Context

Reported as a defect-note by @neo-fable-clio (2026-09-18), seen in neo-agent-institution at engine `dev@70c2c94618`, in framework and consumer build mode: `dist/production/docs/index.html` ends in `Cannot find module './docs/app.mjs'`.

## The Problem

`Neo.worker.App#importApp()` (`src/worker/App.mjs:388`) loads every app through one lazy webpack context, filtered by:

```
/* webpackInclude: /(?:apps|docs\/app|examples|src)\/.*app\.mjs$/ */
```

The docs app's entry is `docs/app.mjs`: the folder `docs/app/` holds its views, and the entry sits beside it. The alternation `docs\/app` followed by `\/.*app\.mjs` needs one more path segment, so the entry never matches. Webpack tests `webpackInclude` against the module's absolute path, not the `./` request (measured by @neo-opus-ada on 2026-03-27, when a `^\.\/` anchor emptied the context). Against absolute paths:

| Path | Today | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| `<neo>/docs/app.mjs` | **false** | true |
| `<neo>/apps/portal/app.mjs` · `<neo>/examples/button/base/app.mjs` · `<neo>/src/…/app.mjs` | true | true |
| `<neo>/app.mjs` | false | false |
| `<neo>/docs/app/…/app.mjs` (no such file today) | true | true |

A context that does not include the entry has no chunk for it, so a bundled App worker cannot import the docs app. The unbundled development mode imports apps as native modules, where magic comments do nothing, which is why working on the docs locally shows nothing wrong.

Since when: #9517 (*Standardize and optimize dynamic imports*) replaced the include `/(?:\/|\\)app.mjs$/`, which matched any `app.mjs`, with the alternation.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/webpack/production/webpack.config.appworker.mjs:155` creates the `Docs` starting point whenever `docs/app` exists, and `buildScripts/build/all.mjs:186` copies `docs/output` and `docs/resources` into `dist/production/docs`. The engine ships the docs app, and its entry cannot load.
- The include decides what a consumer's App worker may contain too, so the fix must stay as narrow as the alternation meant to be: `apps/**`, `examples/**`, `src/**` app entries, plus the one docs entry.

## The Fix

Add the docs entry and keep everything else the include matches: `/(?:(?:apps|docs\/app|examples|src)\/.*|docs\/)app\.mjs$/`. A unit arm pins it against the entries that must match and the paths that must not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit arm reads the include from `src/worker/App.mjs` and tests it against absolute paths, as webpack does. `docs/app.mjs`, `apps/portal/app.mjs`, `examples/button/base/app.mjs` and a `src/…/app.mjs` match; a root `app.mjs` does not. It fails first on `dev`, on the docs entry.
- [ ] A production build of the engine loads `dist/production/docs/index.html` without `Cannot find module './docs/app.mjs'`.

## Out of Scope

- The `webpackExclude` beside it.
- Consumer-mode reach of the engine's own apps (#18868's ticket body records it).
- Workspaces under an `apps/` ancestor match every `app.mjs` below it, today and after the fix. That is the ancestor-name class #17882 closed for the Data worker. It is also why PR #18872's guard, whose fixture sits under `apps/`, cannot witness this defect.

## Related

#9517 (the change that narrowed the include) · #18868 / PR #18872 (the App-worker compile guard, which compiles and so cannot see a context that silently omits an entry) · neomjs/neo-agent-institution#153
